posts.title: This Is Not A Casio AE1200
posts.description: A Blurred Digital Watch That Looks Like a Casio AE1200 Introduction I’m sure some will wonder why I would buy what is an apparent, obvious, blatant even rip-off of the classic Casio AE1200, aka the Casio Royale? I mean the AE1200 is considered a Godly watch at this point. Even more to the point, why would I buy a clone when I actually already own a Casio AE1200? My Casio AE1200 Well, this is a story of my cat-like curiosity. It was a question of if something that was less expensive than the original, tries to look as much as possible like a different watch could possibly be better than the original. Spoiler: for some people it might be a better choice. Meet the Dual Time So, if I haven’t teased things enough, here is the watch in question: Skmei Dual Time The first impression is that this is a clone of the Casio watch. posts.title: My Other Wave Ceptor
posts.description: My Casio Wave Ceptor WVQ-M410 On Wrist. Photo by Unattributed. Introduction I’m embarrassed to admit, I’d almost forgotten about this watch. I bought it at the same time as the other Wave Ceptor that wrote about back in July 1 . It was only recalled when I was cleaning up and organizing my collection a couple of weeks ago and found it, still in the box. But even then, I just took it out of its box, and set on the dresser next to my main watch boxes. Today, however, I picked it up and looked at it. Much to my surprise it had managed to catch a radio signal to synchronize itself to. Since I didn’t have to do anything to adjust it, I decided to give it a wear today. These are my impressions of the watch. The Positives Just like the WVA-M640B, this watch has very nice contrast between the black dial, and the gold colored hands and markers. posts.title: Reliving My Childhood via EDC
posts.description: CJRB Pyrite Lite Button Lock Pocketknife (Photo by Unattributed) NOTE: The tree used in this photo is dead, and the angle makes the blade look like it is in deeper than it actually was. Introduction So, I have to talk a little about the concept of Every Day Carry. This is something that I have become interested in recently. (Recently as in over the last five or six years.) It started, somewhat ironically, when I became interested in getting shoes that weren’t another pair of cheap sneakers, nor another pair of work dress shoes. That’s when I came across a YouTube channel by the name of Rose Anvil 1 . Weston had started making videos where he cut boots and sneakers in half. These videos (originally) were intended to be a stop-gap during the pandemic shutdown. But, they took off and have been a main focus of his YouTube channel ever since.
